issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking a declaration of title need not also claim possession when the property is in judicial custody and the defendant is neither in possession nor able to deliver possession.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought a suit seeking a declaration concerning their title to property and the validity of deeds affecting it.
At the time of suit, the property was attached in a criminal proceeding and was in the magistrate’s custody; no party was in possession.
The defendants were not in possession and could not deliver possession, and the magistrate was not a party to the suit.
The High Court set aside the trial court’s decree because the plaintiffs had not sought recovery of possession, without considering the merits.
issues.conclusion: The suit was competent without a claim for delivery of possession; the appeal was allowed and the case remanded for decision on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1887, the further relief contemplated is relief against the defendant. A plaintiff need not claim possession where the defendant is not in possession and cannot deliver possession, including where the property is in custodia legis. The Court relied on Sunder Singh Mallah Singh Sanatan Dharm High School Trust v. Managing Committee, Sunder Singh-Mallah Singh Rajput High School, Nawab Humayun Begam v. Nawab Shah Mohammad Khan, and K. Sundaresa Iyer v. Sarvajana Sowkiabil Virdhi Nidhi Ltd.; it disapproved Dukkan Ram v. Ram Nanda Singh.

rule.if: declaratory_title_suit and property_in_judicial_custody and defendant_not_in_possession and defendant_unable_to_deliver_possession and custodian_not_a_party

predicates.declaratory_title_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking a declaration of title to property.
predicates.property_in_judicial_custody: The property was held in the custody of a judicial or other legal authority during the suit.
predicates.defendant_not_in_possession: The defendant was not in possession of the property.
predicates.defendant_unable_to_deliver_possession: The defendant was unable to deliver possession of the property to the plaintiff.
predicates.custodian_not_a_party: The authority holding the property in custody was not a party to the suit.

issues.definition: When a title-declaration suit concerns property in judicial custody, the defendant lacks possession and cannot deliver it, and the custodian is not a party, the suit is competent without a claim for possession.
